parameter_notes.location: Global Energy Observatory lists 37.5607 N, -5.3316 E as the Gemasolar plant location. It is used as the project-site point, not claimed as a surveyed tower-centre coordinate.
parameter_notes.altitude_m: PVGIS API DEM elevation = 167 m at the corrected project-site coordinate; source workbook reports 168 m.
parameter_notes.dimensions: 12.305 m horizontal width and 9.752 m height follow Collado/Guallar 2013 and Gemasolar research literature. Repository parameter workbook swaps these labels; HelioCon gives another envelope (11.5 x 10.4 m). Model assumption retained explicitly.
parameter_notes.optical_height_m: Actual tower height is 140 m, confirmed by Sener EPC project page and NLR/SolarPACES. The calculation uses 140 m as nominal optical aiming height above the common mirror-centre datum. Exact receiver equator/pedestal/ground-datum offset is unverified; no invented correction is applied. 116 m is only a rejected literature sensitivity case, not the actual tower height.
parameter_notes.receiver: Finite cylindrical receiver model: radius 4 m and height 10.5 m, based on Sánchez-González et al. 2016 Gemasolar-like case (DOI 10.1016/j.solener.2015.12.055). The actual receiver geometry/aiming strategy is not fully public; nominal centre at 140 m is retained.
parameter_notes.surface: Each mirror is an opaque flat rectangle with azimuth/elevation mount. 115.7 m2 reflective aperture is distributed uniformly inside its envelope; facet gaps and focusing are not traced.
parameter_notes.axes: Interpret dataset x/y as East/North, consistent with published Gemasolar field convention and the north-extended layout; upstream CSV has no explicit axis metadata. Field rotation/survey control remains unverified.
parameter_notes.height: All centres use z=0 relative to a common centre plane. This avoids inventing pedestal elevation; real terrain is unavailable.
parameter_notes.atmosphere: Noone et al. 2012 equation 11; empirical slant-distance transmission assuming about 40 km visibility. Fixed clear-air scenario, not historical local visibility reconstructed from DNI; excludes mirror reflectivity and receiver interception.
parameter_notes.mirror_reflectivity: Literature scenario, not measured Sener reflectivity: Collado & Guallar 2016 Table 1 (doi:10.1016/j.solener.2016.06.065) and Sanchez-Gonzalez et al. (doi:10.1016/j.solener.2015.12.055), case study. Cleanliness=1 and interception=1 in main four-factor result; neither loss is modeled. Separate comparison scenarios may include cleanliness=0.95.
parameter_notes.receiver_optics: Interception integrates an equivalent Gaussian angular beam over the near side of the cylinder. Sun shape 2.51 mrad, slope 2.6 mrad, tracking 2.1 mrad from the cited Gemasolar-like case; receiver solar absorptivity 0.93 from Pérez-Álvarez et al. 2022. These are literature scenarios, not Gemasolar measurements.
parameter_notes.receiver_thermal_efficiency: Literature annual receiver efficiency scenario 0.8916 from Collado & Guallar 2016 Table 1 (RR=4 m, THT=140 m), not a transient thermal balance. It represents absorbed receiver heat after receiver thermal losses; use only for scenario output.

configuration.coordinate_note: Global Energy Observatory 公布的 Gemasolar 电厂场址坐标；用于太阳位置计算，但不解释为塔中心测量控制点。

energy_scope: Only these selected days; no annual field energy estimate
power_scope: Full chain: normal-area reference -> cosine -> joint shadow/blocking -> reflectivity -> cleanliness -> atmosphere -> finite cylindrical receiver interception -> receiver absorptivity -> receiver thermal-efficiency scenario. Optical efficiency ends at receiver incident power; absorbed and net-thermal efficiencies include their stated factors. Neither is electrical output.
loss_accounting: Sequential stage powers are retained for every mirror and close to the normal-area input. Loss percentages use their immediate stage input; do not add percentages.
